proposed_response: Garden-adjacent hobbies include seed saving, botanical sketching or journaling, garden photography, plant propagation, flower arranging, habitat observation, and making labels or supports. Composting can fit if you have space and follow local rules for accepted materials; pressing plants is useful for art or records, but a pressed specimen is not automatically safe to eat. Choose one that matches your climate, space, mobility, budget, and whether you want more growing, observation, craft, or community activity.
rationale: Replaces unsafe culinary use of pressed plants and an unconditional compost claim with a broader, constraint-aware set of related hobbies.

proposed_response: For an at-home extension of cooking, try bread or pastry practice, fermentation with a tested process, regional recipe study, food photography, menu design, or building a family recipe archive. Pick one small project with equipment you already own, such as photographing one dish under different light or testing one bread variable across two batches. An indoor herb or sprout project can add a growing component, while wild foraging does not match the at-home constraint and requires separate identification and land-use knowledge.
rationale: Honors the explicit at-home constraint and replaces casual foraging advice with bounded cooking-related experiments.

proposed_response: Use a stable cabinet or shelf that supports each toy without bending it, limits dust, and keeps valuable pieces away from direct sun, heat, moisture, and large temperature swings. Choose low-heat lighting and limit exposure, because even LEDs do not prevent fading from daylight or all material aging; avoid PVC, adhesive contact, foam, or painted surfaces unless their archival compatibility is known. Keep packaging and loose parts supported rather than under pressure, rotate sensitive items, and maintain dated photographs and an inventory for condition, insurance, or recovery.
rationale: Adds the ultraviolet, material-contact, support, environment, and inventory controls missing from an aesthetics-only display answer.

proposed_response: Choose by the kind of activity you enjoy, nearby access, schedule, cost, weather, social preference, and any mobility or health constraints rather than by a high-intensity label. Low-barrier trials might include walking groups, cycling, swimming, dance, recreational leagues, climbing, paddling, martial arts, or strength classes, with adapted versions available for many of them. Try one short session or beginner course, note enjoyment and recovery the next day, and increase frequency or intensity gradually only if the activity fits your life.
rationale: Removes inaccurate intensity categories and turns a generic list into a practical, access-aware trial process.

proposed_response: PlayStation and Xbox are changing hardware and service ecosystems, so compare the current models rather than relying on a permanent story about exclusives, sales, or graphics. Start with the games you want and where your friends play, then check cross-play, backward compatibility for titles you own, controller and accessibility options, local multiplayer, storage, online requirements, subscription catalog and cancellation terms, disc or digital ownership, PC or cloud support, and total cost. If the deciding games are available on both, controller comfort, used-market access, repair and storage options, and household accounts may matter more than the brand.
rationale: Replaces transient brand stereotypes and sales claims with a current-generation, ownership, accessibility, and cost comparison.

proposed_response: Create an inventory with a stable ID, country or issuing authority, date, denomination, catalog reference, condition note, acquisition source, location, and image, then choose one primary sort such as country and date with tags for themes or sets. Use albums, stock books, mounts, or sleeves made from known archival materials and avoid PVC, pressure, tape, and unknown adhesives; unused stamps with original gum generally should not be hinged. Handle stamps with clean stamp tongs rather than ordinary tweezers, and store the collection in a stable, dry, dark place while checking periodically for moisture, pests, or material change.
rationale: Corrects the hinge and tweezer guidance and adds a durable inventory plus material and environment controls.

proposed_response: Start with the phone or camera you already have, a loaner, or a rental long enough to learn whether you care most about people, wildlife, travel, video, low light, or portability. If buying, set a whole-system budget and compare the exact body plus one suitable lens for autofocus, handling, viewfinder or screen, stabilization, battery, size, accessibility, file workflow, and the future availability and cost of lenses. For used gear, inspect the sensor, lens, controls, ports, battery, mount, autofocus, sample files, shutter count where meaningful, return terms, and whether repair is practical before choosing a specific older model.
rationale: Replaces aging model recommendations with a use-case, system-cost, and used-condition decision process.

proposed_response: Begin by identifying the issuing country, denomination, date, mint mark, metal, expected weight and diameter, edge, and known varieties from a current specialist reference for that series. Compare under good light and magnification, measure with a suitable scale and calipers, document provenance, and learn the common casting, tooling, altered-date, added-mint-mark, and surface-treatment signs without cleaning the coin or using a destructive test. For a valuable or uncertain piece, use an independent specialist or recognized authentication service appropriate to that market, and treat a holder or seller's claim as evidence to verify rather than a guarantee.
rationale: Replaces a US-centric vendor list with non-destructive, series-specific examination and independent escalation while warning against cleaning.

proposed_response: Digital cameras record to a sensor and reusable storage, making review, metadata, copying, and iterative adjustment fast, but batteries, storage, backups, shutters, and equipment still have costs and limits. Film records a latent image on a finite roll that must be developed and usually printed or scanned, so each exposure has a material and processing cost and the result is delayed. Differences in grain, color, contrast, latitude, and sharpness depend on the film stock, format, exposure, chemistry, scan or print, sensor, and processing, so neither medium has one inherent aesthetic or dynamic-range advantage.
rationale: Corrects unlimited and no-extra-cost language and treats film appearance and latitude as process-dependent rather than inherent.

proposed_response: Japan's entry requirements depend on the passport you will use, residence, trip purpose, length of stay, prior status, and sometimes transit or re-entry details, and rules can change before departure. Check the current visa-exemption and entry pages of Japan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the Japanese embassy or consulate responsible for your residence, then verify passport validity, permitted activities, stay length, onward-travel evidence, and any arrival procedures. Do not rely on a general country list until you have matched the rule to your exact passport and travel dates.
rationale: Removes a floating exemption list and usual stay length while giving the exact official, passport-bound verification path.

proposed_response: There is no guaranteed cheapest month because airfare, hotels, school holidays, trade shows, fashion and sporting events, and how early you book can outweigh the season. Search a flexible date grid across several weeks, compare the same neighborhood and room terms, and price the full trip including transport, baggage, airport transfers, heating or air-conditioning needs, attraction closures, and cancellation risk. Late autumn and winter often deserve comparison with peak summer, but verify the exact dates against major events and weather rather than assuming January or February will be cheapest.
rationale: Replaces a fixed-month claim with a reproducible flexible-date and total-cost comparison.

proposed_response: The best time depends on what the group values: mild weather, long daylight, lower cost, indoor culture, gardens, nightlife, or the smallest possible crowds. Compare candidate weeks using historical weather ranges, daylight, airfare and lodging, school and public holidays, major events, attraction hours, and each friend's schedule and heat or cold tolerance; spring and autumn are not automatically quiet or cheap. Agree on two or three priorities and a bad-weather plan, then choose the week that gives the best tradeoff rather than a universal best season.
rationale: Replaces broad seasonal cliches with a group decision based on exact dates, events, costs, and tolerances.

proposed_response: The useful answer depends on the beach's country or region, because seafood, street food, seasonal fruit, and local specialties differ far more than a generic beach menu suggests. Look for a busy, clean vendor serving a regional dish, ask about allergens and ingredients, and choose seafood and other perishables that have been kept at a safe temperature and cooked as expected. Carry water, shade food from heat and sand, and tell me the destination and dietary needs for specific local suggestions.
rationale: Removes US-centric foods, unsupported availability, and a hydration claim while making the recommendation local and food-safety aware.

proposed_response: Start with the tasks you must support, then pack the fewest devices: phone, required charger and cables, and only the laptop, tablet, camera, storage, or headphones you will actually use. A plug adapter changes the plug shape but does not convert voltage, so check every power supply's input range and the destination's plug and voltage before connecting it. Keep lithium batteries and power banks in the permitted carry-on location, protect terminals, check the carrier's current capacity limits, enable device encryption and backups, and avoid putting irreplaceable data on one portable drive.
rationale: Corrects the universal-adapter misconception and adds evidence-led packing, battery-transport, and data-protection guidance.

proposed_response: Sunrise and sunset can give low-angle warm light, and twilight can give cool color, but the best time depends on the mountain's orientation, season, weather, subject, and the shadows you want. Side light can reveal texture, overcast light can simplify contrast, and even midday can work for graphic shapes, clouds, black-and-white, or a viewpoint that is shaded at another time. Scout the sun direction and route, protect highlights, bracket only when the scene needs it, and plan navigation, weather, layers, turnaround time, and a headlamp so the photograph does not require unsafe travel in darkness.
rationale: Replaces a universal golden-hour answer with scene-dependent light choices and the mountain travel plan needed around dawn or dusk.

proposed_response: For many trips, the best combination is walking plus subway or bus, but the answer changes with the boroughs, time, mobility, luggage, weather, and current service. Use the MTA trip planner and service alerts, check whether the specific stations and elevators you need are operating, and compare bus, ferry, commuter rail, bike, taxi, or licensed car service for gaps and late hours. Group nearby stops into one outing and allow transfer time rather than assuming the subway reaches every destination or is always the fastest accessible option.
rationale: Replaces universal efficiency and coverage claims with a multimodal, accessibility- and service-aware route choice.

proposed_response: Options include hotels, business hotels, ryokan, hostels or guesthouses, serviced apartments, licensed private lodging, temple stays in some areas, and capsule hotels for travelers comfortable with their space and rules. Compare the exact location and last transport, room and bed size, private or shared bath, stairs and accessibility, meals, check-in or curfew, luggage storage, language support, cancellation, taxes and fees, and whether the property is legally registered. A ryokan is not automatically expensive or more authentic, and a familiar chain is not automatically consistent, so read the current room and property terms rather than choosing by label alone.
rationale: Removes platform dependence and lodging stereotypes while adding licensing, access, location, and exact-room criteria.

proposed_response: To narrow it down, provide the region, exact dates, party size, tent or vehicle type and length, accessibility needs, pets, budget, and required water, toilet, power, or trail access. Search the official land manager or campground operator first for live availability, reservation windows, site dimensions, road access, seasonal closures, fire and food-storage rules, permits, quiet hours, cancellation, and current alerts; third-party maps are useful leads but not final authority. Keep a legal backup site and do not arrive expecting dispersed camping or a vacant first-come site unless current rules and capacity support it.
rationale: Replaces a generic platform referral with the information and official live checks needed to find a usable, legal campsite.

proposed_response: Choose something tied to a place, maker, or experience you actually enjoyed, such as regional food with a clear label, ceramics, textiles, stationery, tools, music, art, or a small item from a museum or local craft shop. Ask where and by whom it was made, how to care for it, and whether an antique, cultural object, wood, plant, animal material, food, alcohol, or medicine faces export, import, quarantine, or luggage restrictions. Keep receipts and protective packing, avoid assuming a mass-market item is locally made, and check your home country's current customs allowance before purchase.
rationale: Replaces generic cultural-significance claims with provenance, maker support, care, packing, and complete customs checks.

proposed_response: Put practices, matches, travel, and the hardest team sessions on one weekly calendar before adding individual work, because a nominal non-team day may need to be recovery rather than another workout. Choose one or two personal priorities that support the sport, such as strength, aerobic base, speed, or mobility, and place the highest-load work far enough from competition to recover. Track sleep, soreness, motivation, pain, and performance, then reduce volume or intensity when several markers worsen instead of following a fixed moderate-day rule.
rationale: Replaces an automatic non-team-day schedule and generic weakness list with total-load planning and observable recovery feedback.

proposed_response: A leg press moves the hip and knee together while your torso is supported, so it trains several lower-body muscles; the exact emphasis changes with machine geometry, foot position, range, and whether one or both legs work. A leg extension moves mainly at the knee and loads the quadriceps more selectively through a machine-defined arc. Neither is automatically better or corrective: compare adjustability, comfortable range, joint tolerance, available load increments, footprint, and whether the machine supports the program you will follow before buying one for a home gym.
rationale: Corrects exclusive-muscle and bilateral assumptions and frames the choice around mechanics, fit, program, and footprint.

proposed_response: Read the machine's posted instructions or ask gym staff first, because controls and start behavior differ. Stand on the side rails, attach the emergency-stop clip to your clothing, confirm the belt is clear, start at the lowest speed, then step onto the moving belt while holding the rails briefly and looking forward. Walk before changing speed or incline, leave space behind the machine, stop before stepping off, and use the emergency control if you lose position rather than jumping from a fast belt.
rationale: Corrects the dangerous instruction to attach the safety clip to the console and gives a machine-aware start and stop sequence.

proposed_response: Begin with shapes you can enter and leave comfortably, such as mountain pose, a chair-supported fold or balance, tabletop or seated cat-cow, a gentle lunge with support, and a supported rest. Downward-facing dog and child's pose are common but are not comfortable or appropriate for every wrist, knee, shoulder, balance, pregnancy, or blood-pressure situation, so use a wall, chair, blocks, or another pose. Move within a pain-free range, breathe normally, and learn from a qualified beginner teacher when you need individual adaptation.
rationale: Replaces universal benefit claims with accessible starter options and explicit adaptation of commonly difficult poses.

proposed_response: For flexibility, choose two or three movements for the areas you actually want to improve, such as a supported hamstring stretch, low lunge, gentle rotation, or seated or tabletop cat-cow. Enter slowly, stop before sharp, radiating, numb, or unstable sensations, breathe normally, and use support so you can relax rather than force the range. Hold or repeat only as long as it remains comfortable, practice consistently, and track whether ordinary movement improves instead of assuming every beginner should hold the same pose for 30 seconds.
rationale: Removes the fixed hold, maximize-stretch language, and universal Downward Dog prescription in favor of goal- and symptom-based practice.

proposed_response: A supported sit-to-stand is a useful first lower-body exercise for many beginners: use a stable chair, place the feet where you can control them, stand and sit slowly, and use the hands or a higher seat if needed. Choose a comfortable depth and knee and foot path rather than forcing thighs parallel or one posture cue, and stop if pain, dizziness, or loss of control appears. Start with a small number of good repetitions, recover, and build a balanced routine that also includes pulling, pushing, carrying or bracing, and comfortable aerobic activity rather than treating one exercise as a complete program.
rationale: Replaces a universal squat prescription, rigid depth and set count, and incomplete routine with a scalable movement and balanced next step.

proposed_response: Common labels include Hatha, Vinyasa, Iyengar, restorative, Yin, Ashtanga, prenatal, chair, and hot yoga, but studios use those names differently and instructor pace matters as much as the label. Hatha does not always mean gentle, Vinyasa can range from slow to athletic, Ashtanga follows a set progression, and Bikram is one branded form of fixed-sequence heated yoga rather than the definition of all hot yoga. Read the exact class description, temperature, props, pace, and experience level, and choose an unheated or adapted beginner class when heat, pregnancy, medication, balance, or a health condition makes a hot room unsuitable.
rationale: Corrects fixed style stereotypes and distinguishes Bikram from hot yoga while making class and heat selection explicit.

proposed_response: Choose first for reliable grip in your actual practice, enough length and width, stable contact with the floor, and cushioning that helps without making balance feel unstable. Material names such as rubber, PVC, TPE, cork, or polyurethane do not by themselves prove environmental impact, durability, or grip; check full material disclosure, latex sensitivity, odor, cleaning method, expected life, repair or recycling options, and whether a towel is needed for sweat. Try the mat with hands and feet dry and damp if possible, and consider weight, roll size, floor type, joint supports, and accessible markers rather than following one thickness range.
rationale: Removes unsupported eco and thickness rules and replaces them with grip, stability, disclosure, allergy, care, and access criteria.

proposed_response: A kettlebell is a compact weight with a handle above its center of mass, made in fixed or adjustable forms and used for carries, presses, squats, rows, hinges, and ballistic lifts. The offset shape changes grip and leverage compared with a dumbbell, but it does not automatically make an exercise functional, cardiovascular, or better. Choose a weight you can control, learn stable carries, deadlifts, and other slow basics first, protect the floor and surrounding space, and get qualified instruction before high-repetition swings, cleans, or snatches.
rationale: Replaces origin and marketing claims with the actual geometry, use cases, and a safer skill progression for home equipment.

proposed_response: A piano is a specific instrument: an acoustic piano uses hammers and strings, while a digital piano electronically imitates its sound and key response. A keyboard is the broader key-based interface and may be a portable arranger, synthesizer, MIDI controller, organ-style instrument, or digital piano, so electronic keyboards vary from unweighted keys with speakers to weighted actions with no internal sounds. Compare key count and action, pedals, sound source and speakers, polyphony, connections, size, maintenance, headphone use, and the music you want to learn rather than assuming every piano has touch response and every keyboard is light.
rationale: Corrects the acoustic-piano versus generic-keyboard false dichotomy and gives the functional distinctions needed to choose one.

proposed_response: Compare current services in your country using the artists and recordings you actually want, because catalogs, prices, plans, audio formats, and device support change and some music stores are not equivalent to an all-you-can-stream subscription. Check total household cost, ads and offline limits, lossless or spatial support you can use, recommendation and library tools, uploads, lyrics, accessibility, parental controls, cancellation and export options, privacy, and whether your speakers or car work without a fragile workaround. Trial the leading two with the same playlist and devices, then keep the one that handles discovery, ownership expectations, and playback reliably.
rationale: Replaces a transient brand list and incomparable Bandcamp category with a current, region- and catalog-specific service trial.

proposed_response: A good concert system delivers even coverage, clear vocals and instruments, controlled low frequencies, useful headroom, and consistent timing and tonal balance across the audience rather than simply being loud. That depends on speaker placement and aiming, room and stage acoustics, delay alignment, microphones, monitor strategy, gain before feedback, system processing, and an engineer mixing for the performance. The result should preserve impact without persistent distortion or needlessly hazardous sound levels; as an attendee, well-fitted hearing protection can reduce exposure while retaining more clarity than improvised plugs.
rationale: Replaces vague high-dynamic-range language with the system, room, mix, feedback, and hearing-level factors that determine concert sound.

proposed_response: Follow the official calendars and mailing lists of nearby venues, promoters, festivals, record shops, arts organizations, and artists you care about, then add a local events calendar or concert-discovery service for breadth. Search by a travel radius and date range, but verify the event, age and access rules, venue, on-sale time, fees, refund policy, and authorized seller on the venue or artist's current page before paying. Use alerts sparingly and review their location and contact-data permissions, and treat social posts, resale links, and direct messages as leads rather than proof that a ticket is valid.
rationale: Replaces a platform-first list with primary event verification, accessibility and fee checks, privacy, and ticket-fraud resistance.

proposed_response: Flute, clarinet, saxophone, recorder, trumpet, trombone, oboe, and bassoon are familiar wind instruments; saxophones and clarinets are woodwinds even though their bodies are usually metal or wood-based composites, while trumpets and trombones are brass. A good beginner choice depends on the music, available teacher or ensemble, instrument size and weight, breath and embouchure demands, hand reach, noise, maintenance, and rental or repair access. Try a properly maintained instrument with a teacher or rental program rather than assuming flute and saxophone are equally accessible to every beginner.
rationale: Answers with common examples while correcting accessibility assumptions and explaining the woodwind/brass distinction and fit factors.

proposed_response: "World music" groups many unrelated traditions and industries, so it is more useful to explore a place, language, instrument, scene, or musical feature. Possible starting points include West African highlife and Afrobeat, contemporary Afrobeats, Hindustani or Carnatic traditions, Indonesian gamelan, Arabic maqam-based music, flamenco, reggae and dub, son cubano, Brazilian choro or samba, Korean popular music, or any local tradition represented by knowledgeable artists and labels. Note that Afrobeat and Afrobeats are distinct histories and styles, then follow the musicians, region, and context rather than treating each genre as one exotic soundscape.
rationale: Replaces cultural shorthand and genre stereotypes with regionally specific starting points and a key Afrobeat/Afrobeats distinction.

proposed_response: Check the artist and venue policy for phones, interchangeable-lens cameras, lens length, flash, bags, credentials, and where you may stand, and respect other attendees' view and privacy. In low light, use the widest usable aperture, a shutter speed fast enough for the performer's motion, auto ISO within a quality limit you accept, continuous autofocus, short bursts, and negative exposure compensation when bright stage lights would fool the meter; avoid flash unless explicitly permitted and appropriate. Shoot a few frames, review highlights rather than every image, protect your hearing and equipment, and keep awareness of staff, cables, crowd movement, and exits.
rationale: Keeps policy-first advice while making exposure settings conditional and adding audience, privacy, hearing, and situational constraints.

proposed_response: Electronic music spans ambient, house, techno, drum and bass, electro, trance, dubstep, synth-pop, IDM, garage, footwork, and many regional scenes, so start with the rhythm, intensity, vocals, era, or listening setting you want. For example, compare one ambient record, one house or techno DJ set, and one bass-focused or experimental release, then follow the artists, labels, collaborators, and mixes from the one you enjoy. Give me two tracks you like and one you do not, and I can suggest a more precise path without calling older releases modern or treating a few famous albums as the whole field.
rationale: Replaces a small dated album list with a durable subgenre experiment and preference-led recommendation path.

proposed_response: For travel outside open, patrolled terrain, read the regional avalanche forecast for the exact zone and elevation, identify the avalanche problems and terrain on the route, and be willing to choose lower-consequence terrain or cancel. A transceiver, probe, and shovel are companion-rescue tools, not protection from burial, and every member needs practiced search, rescue, first-aid, communication, and route-decision skills; do not rely on carrying gear or traveling alone. If that training and local judgment are not already in place, use open terrain controlled by the ski area or hire a qualified local guide, and obey closures even when nearby tracks are visible.
rationale: Corrects the gear-as-safety implication and centers terrain avoidance, practiced companion rescue, group travel, and closures.

proposed_response: I need your city or coordinates, country, and the meaning of "tonight" in local time, and I still cannot verify live radar or warnings from here. Check the official national weather service and local emergency alerts for the hazard type, timing, affected area, confidence, and whether a watch, warning, or evacuation instruction is active; a general app icon is not enough. Charge devices, enable alerts, know the safest nearby shelter for the named hazard, and share the official alert text if you want help interpreting it.
rationale: Keeps the real-time boundary while adding the missing time zone, alert semantics, immediate preparation, and an interpretation path.

proposed_response: A heat wave is a sustained period of unusually hot conditions for a particular place and season, often defined by the local weather authority, so feeling hot for one day does not establish one. Check the official forecast and heat alerts for your location, including overnight lows, humidity or heat index where used, duration, and local thresholds. Move to a cooler place, reduce exertion, drink according to your needs, and seek urgent help for confusion, fainting, seizures, severe weakness, or other signs of serious heat illness rather than waiting for the label.
rationale: Defines heat wave relative to local climatology and adds proportionate action for a user who may be describing personal heat exposure.

proposed_response: There is no single answer until "sunniest" is defined as measured sunshine duration, percentage of possible sunshine, cloud-free days, or solar energy, over a specified station and record period. Yuma, Arizona, is often cited for very high recorded sunshine duration, while parts of the Atacama Desert stand out under cloudiness and solar-radiation measures. A defensible ranking should name the metric, station, observation period, missing-data treatment, and source instead of combining hours and clear-day claims into one world record.
rationale: Removes unsupported numeric superlatives and explains why Yuma and the Atacama can lead under different meteorological measures.

proposed_response: I need the city or coordinates, country, and the start and end time meant by "last night," and I cannot verify a live local total from here. Use the official weather service or a nearby quality-controlled station and distinguish new snowfall from snow depth already on the ground, because wind, melting, compaction, elevation, and observation time can make nearby reports differ. Share the station, time window, and reported value and I can help interpret whether it represents your neighborhood.
rationale: Goes beyond a generic referral by defining the location, time window, and snowfall-versus-depth evidence needed for a meaningful local answer.

proposed_response: Rain can supply crop and pasture water, refill soil moisture, and reduce irrigation demand, but its effect depends on crop, growth stage, soil, slope, drainage, temperature, disease pressure, and what came before and after it. Too little can stress plants, while intense, prolonged, or badly timed rain can cause runoff, erosion, waterlogging, nutrient loss, lodging, disease, pollination problems, and delayed field work or harvest. Even a moderate total may help one field and harm another, so a useful local answer needs the crop, recent soil moisture, forecast amount and intensity, and farm conditions.
rationale: Removes the universal moderate-rain benefit and explains the crop-, stage-, intensity-, and field-dependent mechanisms.

proposed_response: Not every storm receives an official name. Tropical cyclones are named under regional procedures using predetermined lists coordinated by meteorological authorities, with rules for when a system qualifies, how names are reused, and when a destructive name is retired. Winter and other non-tropical storm names may come from a national service, regional partnership, or private media organization and may not be official everywhere, so first identify the storm type and naming authority.
rationale: Corrects the implication that all storms use one WMO rotation and distinguishes official regional tropical naming from variable non-tropical practices.

proposed_response: I need your location and local time, and I cannot read a live outdoor sensor or current weather feed from here. Check the official weather service or a nearby reporting station and note its observation time and distance, since an airport, shaded home sensor, sunlit car, and phone estimate can differ. Share the reported temperature, humidity, wind, and what you are planning to do, and I can help interpret how it may feel and what conditions matter.
rationale: Preserves the live-data boundary while adding observation context and a useful interpretation path.

proposed_response: I need your city or coordinates, country, and time window, and I cannot verify live radar, forecast, or warnings from here. Check the official weather service and local emergency alerts for the specific hazard, arrival window, affected area, and any watch, warning, shelter, or evacuation instruction, then avoid relying on one app's generic storm symbol. Enable alerts, charge devices, secure or move what is safe to handle before conditions worsen, know the appropriate shelter, and share the official alert text if you want help interpreting it.
rationale: Replaces a generic news-app referral and premature emergency-services instruction with location, hazard, official alert, preparation, and interpretation steps.
